speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have there been any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the timing of the diarrhea relative to your levofloxacin treatment is highly suggestive of antibiotic-associated *C. difficile* infection. Have you noticed any significant dehydration, such as dizziness or reduced urine output, and has anyone in your household recently developed similar gastrointestinal symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI). I am requesting stool testing for *C. difficile* toxins and a stool culture to confirm.
